notes:
Status: closed-lost -> self-host. Short summary: Emberstone is a large payment processor with strict residency and deep cost scrutiny. After security sign-off requirements (SAML SSO, KMS, audit logs) and procurement freeze in Q1, the infra org accelerated a self-host PoC using vLLM + TGI + TensorRT-LLM to keep models and keys inside their VPC and to minimize per-token spend. Key quotes: "We need full control of KV cache and HSM access"; "If we can get < $0.0005/token at scale we will keep it in-house".

Why lost:
- Procurement cost freeze delayed commitment; internal infra argued self-host would be cheaper long-term once optimized (quantization + TensorRT).
- Security/legal preferred customer-managed KMS and air-gapped lanes for key ops; Redwood hosted options required further contract/legal work they didn't want to wait on.
- No executive sponsor after payments org reorg; champion left prior to final signoff.

Technical requirements they prioritized:
- Throughput target ~200 req/s for embeddings-retrieval + 50 req/s chat peak, p95 latency goal ~50-150ms depending on model.
- Preferred model family: Llama2-70B quantized / mix of open-weight models.
- Strong interest in prefix/KV caching, automatic batching, and CUDA/TensorRT kernels for cost reduction.

Engagement notes and follow-ups:
- SE (Priya) did two deep POC sessions showing Redwood Optimize recommendations; infra team counters with their own cost models using TF32/TensorRT quantized runtimes.
- Legal asked for ISO27001 + dedicated SOC2 timeline; provided Redwood security FAQ but procurement timeline slipped.
- Next: keep warm; track self-host pilot metrics; if pilot shows stability/cost issues, re-engage with focused win-back playbook (cost comparison, migration plan, Hybrid private control plane option).
